notes: Remember this device, on the owner panel. The player card in Players is now sized from the window instead of a fixed 214x318, so it grows with the panel whether Scale UI contents is on or off. Off by default. With it on, the first publish the endpoint actually accepts writes Aether/publish.dkey - the token, the account, the executor and a hardware id where the executor reports one - and a later load reads it, checks the account and device, and unlocks publishing with the box already filled. Nothing is written before a successful call, so a typo is never persisted; if the endpoint ever answers 401 to the stored token the file is deleted and the box cleared, so a rotated token cannot fail silently forever. Forget this device removes it. Being honest about the limit: the file is plaintext and a local check is a local claim - it stops the token being lifted to another account or machine, not someone reading this executor's workspace, and another script in the same executor could write the same file. A credential that cannot be forged or shared has to be issued and verified by the Worker.
